name: name_to_handle_at
synopsis: int name_to_handle_at(int dirfd, const char *pathname, struct file_handle *handle, int *mount_id, int flags);
int open_by_handle_at(int mount_fd, struct file_handle *handle, int flags);
description: The name_to_handle_at() system call returns a file handle and mount ID for a specified file path. The open_by_handle_at() system call uses this handle to open the file and return a file descriptor.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Pointer to structure for file handle

parameters.name: mount_id
parameters.description: Pointer to return the mount ID

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags such as AT_EMPTY_PATH or AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW

return_value.success: name_to_handle_at() returns 0; open_by_handle_at() returns a file descriptor
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, errno is set

errors.description: pathname, mount_id, or handle points outside your accessible address space
flags includes an invalid bit value or handle->handle_bytes is greater than MAX_HANDLE_SZ
pathname is an empty string but AT_EMPTY_PATH was not specified in flags
The file descriptor in dirfd does not refer to a directory and conditions for AT_EMPTY_PATH are not met
The filesystem does not support decoding of a pathname to a file handle
The handle->handle_bytes value passed into the call was too small
For open_by_handle_at(), mount_fd is not an open file descriptor
For open_by_handle_at(), the caller does not have the CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH capability
For open_by_handle_at(), the specified handle is not valid
